items.title: Harry Shields Interview, 1961-05-28
items.q: I had a brother between Larry and I, played piano. Edward.

ctx.x: Yeah. Um, are they still living by any chance? No, no. They died. And how much older was, uh, Larry than, uh, you? Six years. Six years. I think we have, uh, several accounts of his life. You know, the jazz club had the whole issue.

I had a brother between Larry and I, played piano. Edward. Edward. I think you played with him, didn't you, John? Did you know him? Ed, the piano player? He played with Sharky and, uh, he played with Emmett too. Oh. And, uh, we had a little band with Emmett. I think I heard him. Ed played piano. Sure. And we had Charlie Leach on drums then. And, uh, oh, uh, let's see, Donald Coleman on violin. You remember Don.
Donald Coleman, he was the president of the Times-Picay Union, right? Right, right. That's right. And, uh... What did he play? Violin. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah.
